mainTopic: Fire damage and the height of the נר חנוכה; then the opening of פרק מרובה on תשלומי כפל and ארבעה וחמשה and which items כפל covers.
overview: The amud opens with the end of פרק הכונס. A blacksmith is liable for damage done by a spark from his hammer. If a camel's flax pokes into a store and catches fire from the storekeeper's lamp, the camel owner pays. If the storekeeper put his lamp outside, the storekeeper pays, but רבי יהודה exempts him when it was a נר חנוכה. רבא tries to prove from this that a נר חנוכה belongs below ten טפחים. The גמרא rejects the proof, because חז"ל did not burden someone doing a מצוה to place the lamp that high. A further teaching rules that a נר חנוכה placed above twenty אמות is פסולה, like a סוכה and a מבוי. After the הדרן, פרק מרובה begins with a משנה: תשלומי כפל applies to any stolen item, but ארבעה וחמשה applies only to an ox or a sheep, and neither fine applies to someone who steals from a thief. The גמרא discusses whether the משנה supports רבי יוחנן's ruling on a טוען טענת גנב. It then learns the scope of כפל from a כלל ופרט וכלל and begins asking whether birds are included, a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A blacksmith's spark that causes damage
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a spark flies out from under a blacksmith's hammer and causes damage, the blacksmith is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: If a spark flew out from under the hammer and caused damage, the one hammering is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a simple case. A blacksmith's spark causes damage, and he has to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the blacksmith was doing normal work, he is responsible for the spark his hammering produced. The spark is treated as the result of his own action.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A spark that came out from under the hammer
and caused damage: he is liable.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is liable for damage caused by a spark from his hammer.

steps.title: A flax-laden camel catches fire in a store
steps.stepSummary: A camel carrying flax walks through the public street. Its flax goes into a store, catches fire from the storekeeper's lamp, and burns the building. The camel's owner is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: A camel was loaded with flax and passed through the public domain. Its flax went into a store, caught fire from the storekeeper's lamp, and set the building on fire. The camel's owner is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second fire case. A camel's flax pokes into a store and catches fire from a lamp inside, and the camel's owner must pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The storekeeper had every right to keep his lamp inside his own store. It was the camel owner's flax that went into the store, so the blame falls on him.

keyTerms.meaning: The public domain, a public street

phrases.english: A camel that was loaded with flax,
and passed through the public domain,
and its flax went into the store
and caught fire from the storekeeper's lamp,
and it set the building on fire:
the camel's owner is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case of fire damage in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the lamp is inside the store, the camel owner is liable for the fire.

steps.title: When the storekeeper put his lamp outside
steps.stepSummary: If the storekeeper placed his lamp outside in the street, he is the one who is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the storekeeper placed his lamp outside, the storekeeper is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה changes one detail: now the lamp is outside the store. This time the storekeeper is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting a burning lamp out in the public street is careless, because people and animals pass by there. So the blame moves from the camel owner to the storekeeper.

phrases.english: If the storekeeper placed his lamp outside,
the storekeeper is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes the location of the lamp, which reverses who is liable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A storekeeper who places his lamp in the public street is liable for the fire it causes.

steps.title: רבי יהודה exempts a נר חנוכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that if the lamp outside was a נר חנוכה, the storekeeper is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if it was a נר חנוכה, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds an exception to the last case. If the outside lamp was a נר חנוכה, the storekeeper does not pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of נר חנוכה is to place it outside, so the storekeeper had permission to put it there. Because of that, he is not considered careless.
steps.whatToRemember: Lamp inside: the camel owner pays. Lamp outside: the storekeeper pays. But according to רבי יהודה, if the outside lamp is a נר חנוכה, the storekeeper is פטור.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole גמרא that follows is built on this one line of רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
With a Chanukah lamp, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בְּנֵר חֲנוּכָּה פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An exception to the ruling in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A storekeeper whose outside lamp was a נר חנוכה is exempt.

steps.title: רבא's inference: a נר חנוכה belongs below ten טפחים
steps.stepSummary: רבינא, quoting רבא, says that we can learn from רבי יהודה that the מצוה is to place the נר חנוכה within ten טפחים of the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבינא said in the name of רבא: Learn from רבי יהודה that the נר חנוכה should be placed within ten טפחים of the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a claim: רבי יהודה's ruling teaches a halacha about the height of the נר חנוכה. This step states the conclusion, and the next step gives the reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא is drawing a practical halacha about נר חנוכה out of a case about fire damage. He says the מצוה is to place it low, below ten טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: Within ten טפחים of the ground

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Ravina said in the name of Rava:
Learn from Rabbi Yehuda's ruling

phrases.aramaic: נֵר חֲנוּכָּה – מִצְוָה לְהַנִּיחָהּ בְּתוֹךְ עֲשָׂרָה.
phrases.english: that the מצוה of a Chanukah lamp is to place it within ten.
phrases.notes: "Ten" means ten טפחים (handbreadths) up from the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a halacha about נר חנוכה out of רבי יהודה's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The מצוה is to place the נר חנוכה below ten טפחים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's exemption for a נר חנוכה in the משנה.

steps.title: Why the exemption proves the lamp must be low
steps.stepSummary: If the lamp could be placed higher than ten טפחים, the camel owner could say: 'You should have placed it above the camel and its rider.' Since רבי יהודה still exempts the storekeeper, the lamp must belong down low.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think it may be placed above ten, why would רבי יהודה exempt the storekeeper? Let the camel owner say: 'You should have put it higher than a camel and its rider!' So must we not conclude that the מצוה is to place it within ten?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבא's proof. If placing the lamp high were allowed, the storekeeper would still be at fault for putting it low.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An exemption only makes sense if the storekeeper had no better option. If he could have done the מצוה with the lamp above the camel's reach, putting it low would be careless. Since רבי יהודה exempts him, low must be the correct way to do the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: If it would enter your mind (if you think)

phrases.english: For if you think it may be placed above ten,
why did Rabbi Yehuda say
that with a Chanukah lamp he is exempt?
Let him say to him:
phrases.notes: Let the camel owner say this to the storekeeper.

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְאַנּוֹחַהּ לְמַעְלָה מִגָּמָל וְרוֹכְבוֹ!
phrases.english: You should have placed it above a camel and its rider!
Rather, must we not conclude from this
that the מצוה is to place it within ten?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the inference in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: A נר חנוכה should be placed below ten טפחים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The exemption would make no sense if the storekeeper could have placed the lamp above the camel's reach.

steps.title: Rejection: חז"ל did not burden someone doing a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's proof. Even if the lamp may be placed above ten, the storekeeper is still exempt. Since he is doing a מצוה, חז"ל did not make him go to the trouble of placing it above a camel and its rider.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: No. Really, I can tell you it may be placed even above ten. As for what you said, that he should have placed it above a camel and its rider: since he is busy with a מצוה, the Rabbis did not burden him that much.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof. רבי יהודה's exemption can be explained even if the lamp is allowed to be placed high.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed that if high placement is allowed, the storekeeper must use it. The גמרא answers that placing a lamp that high would be very hard, and חז"ל did not demand that much effort from someone doing a מצוה. So the exemption proves nothing about the ten-טפחים rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis did not burden him

steps.whatToRemember: רבא wanted to prove that a נר חנוכה must be below ten טפחים. The גמרא rejects the proof: the storekeeper is exempt simply because חז"ל did not burden someone doing a מצוה to place it so high.
steps.confusionAlert: The rejection does not say a נר חנוכה must be placed above ten. It only shows that this משנה does not prove it must be below ten.

phrases.english: They say: No.

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ אֲפִילּוּ לְמַעְלָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה,
phrases.english: Really, I can tell you it may be even above ten,
and as for what you said,

phrases.aramaic: אִבְּעִי לָךְ לְאַנּוֹחַהּ לְמַעְלָה מִגָּמָל וְרוֹכְבוֹ?
phrases.english: 'You should have placed it above a camel and its rider':
since he is busy doing a מצוה,
the Rabbis did not burden him this much.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof given in steps 5 and 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof itself, not necessarily the halacha that the lamp belongs below ten.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that if high placement is allowed, the storekeeper must use it. But חז"ל did not require that much effort from someone doing a מצוה.

steps.title: A נר חנוכה above twenty אמות is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא reports, in the name of רבי תנחום, that a נר חנוכה placed higher than twenty אמות is פסולה, just like a סוכה and a מבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: רב נתן בר מניומי taught in the name of רבי תנחום: a נר חנוכה placed higher than twenty אמות is invalid, like a סוכה and like a מבוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more rule about the height of a נר חנוכה. This time it sets the top limit instead of the bottom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5-7 asked whether the lamp must be placed below ten טפחים, and that question was left open. This statement sets a clear upper limit: above twenty אמות the lamp does not count for the מצוה. It uses the same twenty-אמה limit that applies to a סוכה and to the beam over a מבוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Twenty cubits, the top height limit
Invalid; it does not count for the מצוה
The booth for סוכות, which is also invalid above twenty אמות
An alleyway, whose crossbeam does not work above twenty אמות

steps.whatToRemember: The bottom limit of ten טפחים was not proven, but the top limit is clear: a נר חנוכה above twenty אמות is פסולה, like a סוכה and a מבוי.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the measurements. Ten טפחים (handbreadths) is a low height, and twenty אמות (cubits) is very high.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said
Rav Natan bar Minyumi taught
in the name of Rabbi Tanchum
A Chanukah lamp that one placed
higher than twenty amos
is invalid
like a sukkah and like an alleyway.
phrases.notes: A סוכה taller than twenty אמות is invalid, and so is a crossbeam over a מבוי placed higher than that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא, דָּרֵשׁ רַב נָתָן בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי תַּנְחוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof for a ten-טפחים maximum was rejected, this step gives a clear upper height limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נר חנוכה placed above twenty אמות is פסולה, like a סוכה and a מבוי.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק הכונס
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing formula that ends פרק הכונס.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק הכונס.
steps.whatsHappening: This line ends the sixth chapter, פרק הכונס. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a short farewell that is said at the end of every פרק. After it, the topic changes completely, from damages done by fire to the fines a גנב pays.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the farewell said at the end of a chapter
The name of the chapter that is now ending

phrases.english: We will return to you, Hakoneis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after its final sugya.

steps.title: Double payment covers more cases than four- and five-fold payment
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens with a משנה: תשלומי כפל applies to anything stolen, but תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה applies only to an ox or a sheep, based on the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule of double payment covers more than the rule of four- and five-fold payment. Double payment applies both to living things and to non-living things. Four- and five-fold payment applies only to an ox or a sheep, as the פסוק says: 'If a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter, פרק מרובה, begins with a משנה. It compares two fines that a גנב pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גנב who is caught pays כפל, double the value, and this applies to any item, living or not. If he stole an ox or a sheep and then slaughtered or sold it, he pays more: five times for an ox and four times for a sheep. The words 'ox or sheep' in the פסוק limit that bigger fine to just those two animals.

keyTerms.meaning: Covers more; it is also the name of this new פרק
Double payment, the fine a thief pays
Four- or five-fold payment, for slaughtering or selling a stolen sheep or ox
The breath of life; a living creature

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets out the two main fines for theft, and the rest of the פרק builds on them.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: Broader
is the rule of double payment
than the rule of four- and five-fold payment.
For the rule of double payment applies

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּדָבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ רוּחַ חַיִּים
phrases.english: both to something that has the breath of life

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ רוּחַ חַיִּים
phrases.english: and to something that has no breath of life,
but the rule of four- and five-fold payment
applies only
to an ox and a sheep alone,
as it is said:
"If a man steals an ox or a sheep
and slaughters it or sells it, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: מְרוּבָּה מִדַּת תַּשְׁלוּמֵי כֶפֶל מִמִּדַּת תַּשְׁלוּמֵי אַרְבָּעָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כפל applies to all stolen items, but ארבעה וחמשה applies only to an ox or a sheep.

steps.title: Stealing from a thief brings no extra fines
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: someone who steals from a thief does not pay כפל, and someone who slaughters or sells an animal after it was already stolen does not pay ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who steals after a thief already stole the item does not pay double payment. One who slaughters or sells an animal after a thief already stole it does not pay four- and five-fold payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds another limit. The extra fines apply only to the first thief, not to a second person who takes the item from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous line limited ארבעה וחמשה to certain animals. This line limits both fines to certain people: a second thief who takes an item that was already stolen is not fined. The משנה only rules out the extra payments here. It does not say the second thief owes nothing at all.

keyTerms.meaning: One who steals from a thief, taking something already stolen

steps.whatToRemember: There are two limits. ארבעה וחמשה applies only to an ox or a sheep. Neither extra fine applies to someone who steals from a thief.

phrases.english: One who steals after the thief does not
pay double payment,
nor does the one who slaughters or the one who sells
after the thief
pay four- and five-fold payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין הַגּוֹנֵב אַחַר הַגַּנָּב מְשַׁלֵּם תַּשְׁלוּמֵי כֶפֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a second limit on the theft fines.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A second thief who steals from the first thief is not fined כפל, and one who slaughters or sells an already-stolen animal is not fined ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: The משנה did not list the טוען טענת גנב difference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the משנה did not teach a difference between כפל and ארבעה וחמשה in the case of a טוען טענת גנב.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: But the משנה does not teach this: 'double payment applies both to a thief and to one who falsely claims a thief stole it, while four and five payments apply only to a thief.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by noticing something the משנה left out. This is a setup line that prepares a proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave one way that כפל is broader than ארבעה וחמשה: it applies to living and non-living things. If a טוען טענת גנב paid only כפל and not ארבעה וחמשה, that would be a second way כפל is broader. The משנה did not mention it, and the next step draws a conclusion from that silence.

keyTerms.meaning: Double payment that a thief pays
Four or five times the value, paid for slaughtering or selling a stolen sheep or ox
A guardian who falsely claims that a thief stole the deposit he was watching

phrases.english: GEMARA: But this:
phrases.notes: The words in quotation marks that follow are not in the משנה. The גמרא is describing a line the משנה could have said but did not.

phrases.english: 'the rule of double payment applies

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּגַנָּב בֵּין בְּטוֹעֵן טַעֲנַת גַּנָּב,
phrases.english: both to a thief and to one who claims a thief's claim,
while the rule of four and five payments
applies only to a thief alone'
it does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ ״מִדַּת תַּשְׁלוּמֵי כֶפֶל נוֹהֶגֶת בֵּין בְּגַנָּב בֵּין בְּטוֹעֵן טַעֲנַת גַּנָּב״ לָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's discussion of the new משנה by noticing what the משנה's list of differences leaves out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's list of ways כפל is broader does not include the case of a טוען טענת גנב.

steps.title: The silence supports רבי חייא בר אבא
steps.stepSummary: Because the משנה did not list that difference, it supports רבי חייא בר אבא in the name of רבי יוחנן: a טוען טענת גנב pays כפל, and if he slaughtered or sold the animal he pays ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי חייא בר אבא, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן: one who falsely claims that a thief stole a deposit pays double. If he slaughtered or sold it, he pays four and five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the משנה's silence as a proof for the view of רבי חייא בר אבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a טוען טענת גנב paid only כפל, the משנה would have listed that as another way כפל is broader. Since it did not, he must pay ארבעה וחמשה too. That is exactly what רבי יוחנן rules.

keyTerms.meaning: A deposit left with a guardian
He slaughtered or sold the animal

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that a dishonest guardian who claims theft is treated like a real thief for ארבעה וחמשה as well as for כפל.

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: for Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
One who claims a thief's claim about a deposit
phrases.notes: He says a thief took it, but it turns out he took it himself.

phrases.english: pays double payment.
If he slaughtered or sold it,
he pays four and five payments.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the missing case noted in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חייא בר אבא's ruling, in the name of רבי יוחנן, that a טוען טענת גנב pays ארבעה וחמשה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's silence: it did not list this case as a way כפל is broader than ארבעה וחמשה

steps.title: Second version: shall we say the משנה supports him?
steps.stepSummary: A second version presents the same support only as a tentative suggestion: 'shall we say' the משנה supports רבי חייא בר אבא?
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the discussion went like this: Shall we say this supports רבי חייא בר אבא, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן: one who falsely claims that a thief stole a deposit pays double, and if he slaughtered or sold it he pays four and five?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the discussion. Here the proof is only suggested with 'לימא', which sets up a rejection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling quoted is word for word the same as in step 13. The only change is the opening word לימא ('shall we say'). That word warns us the proof is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say: a suggested proof that is usually rejected

steps.confusionAlert: There are two versions here, not one argument. In the first version the support stands. In the second version, which starts with 'לימא', the support is rejected.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא –
phrases.english: Shall we say this supports Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: for Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
One who claims a thief's claim about a deposit
pays double payment.
If he slaughtered or sold it,
he pays four and five payments?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: לֵימָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the proof from step 13 as a tentative suggestion in a second version of the discussion.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חייא בר אבא's ruling that a טוען טענת גנב pays ארבעה וחמשה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's silence about a difference in the case of a טוען טענת גנב

steps.title: The משנה said 'broader', not 'the only difference'
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The משנה only said that כפל is broader (מרובה). It never claimed to list every difference, so the תנא could have taught one example and left out others.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the משנה say 'there is no difference except…'? It says 'is broader.' The תנא taught one case and left others out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from the משנה's silence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proof from silence only works if the משנה claims to give a complete list, as the wording 'אין בין' ('the only difference is') would. The משנה said 'מרובה', which just shows that כפל covers more and gives one example. So leaving out the טוען טענת גנב case proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'There is no difference except…': wording that signals a complete list
Broader, covering more; the opening word of the משנה
The תנא taught some cases and left others out

steps.whatToRemember: In the second version, the משנה gives no proof for רבי חייא בר אבא. Because it says 'מרובה' and not 'אין בין', its list need not be complete: תנא ושייר.

phrases.english: Does it teach: 'There is no difference between…'?!
phrases.notes: That wording would mean the משנה is giving the complete list of differences.

phrases.english: It teaches 'is broader,'
it taught one case and left others out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the tentative proof suggested in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה. רבי יוחנן's ruling itself is not refuted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה gives a complete list of differences. Its wording 'מרובה' does not promise that, so the missing case can be explained by תנא ושייר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's silence about the טוען טענת גנב is not a proof either way.

steps.title: Where does the scope of double payment come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about how widely תשלומי כפל applies and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'For the rule of תשלומי כפל applies…' From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the line in the משנה that says the rule of כפל applies widely. It asks where in the תורה this comes from. This line sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps compared כפל with ארבעה וחמשה. Now the גמרא wants the actual source that tells us which kinds of items get כפל.

keyTerms.meaning: Double payment, the fine a thief pays
Here: the rule, or the measure of how a law applies
From where are these matters derived? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: For the rule of double payment applies, etc.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the כפל versus ארבעה וחמשה discussion and returns to an earlier line of the משנה to find its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that defines which items are subject to תשלומי כפל.

steps.title: The verse is read as general, specific, general
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק of כפל as a כלל ופרט וכלל. It concludes that כפל covers any movable item that has money value in itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'For any matter of trespass' is a general statement. 'For an ox, a donkey, a sheep, or a garment' is a list of specifics. 'For any lost item' is another general statement. When a general statement, specifics, and a general statement come together, you include only things similar to the specifics. The specifics are movable and worth money in themselves, so the rule covers anything movable and worth money in itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The ברייתא splits the פסוק into general, specific, and general parts. It then uses the rule for that pattern to find what all the listed items have in common.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the rule of כלל ופרט וכלל, the law reaches past the four listed items, but only to things that share their key feature. The ברייתא says that feature is being movable (מטלטל) and being worth money in itself (גופו ממון).

keyTerms.meaning: General, specific, general: a method of reading a פסוק
The item itself is worth money

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic boundary of which stolen items get כפל. The next step depends on it.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"For any matter of trespass" is a generalization,
"for an ox, for a donkey,
for a sheep, and for a garment" is a detail,
"for any lost item" again generalizes;
a generalization, a detail, and a generalization:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט;
phrases.english: you may include only what is similar to the detail;
just as the detail is clearly defined as
an item that is movable and is itself money,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל דָּבָר הַמִּטַּלְטֵל וְגוּפוֹ מָמוֹן.
phrases.english: so too any item that is movable and is itself money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק is a כלל ופרט וכלל, so כפל applies to any movable item that is worth money in itself.

steps.title: What the rule leaves out: land, slaves, documents, and consecrated property
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists what falls outside כפל: קרקעות, עבדים, שטרות, and הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Land is excluded because it cannot be moved. Slaves are excluded because the תורה compares them to land. Documents are excluded because, even though they can be moved, they are not worth money in themselves. Consecrated property is excluded because the פסוק says 'his fellow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now applies its rule and names four things that do not get כפל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land fails the 'movable' test. Slaves fail it too, because the תורה treats them like land. Documents are movable, but they fail the 'worth money in itself' test, since their value lies in what they prove. הקדש is left out for a different reason: the word רעהו shows that the payment goes to another person, not to the Temple.

keyTerms.meaning: Were compared, treated as equal in law

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that הקדש is not excluded by the 'movable and worth money' rule. It is excluded by a separate word in the פסוק, רעהו.

phrases.english: Land is excluded, since it is not movable;
slaves are excluded, since they are compared to land;
documents are excluded,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּטַּלְטְלִין, אֵין גּוּפָן מָמוֹן;
phrases.english: since even though they are movable, they are not themselves money;
phrases.notes: The paper itself is worth almost nothing. What matters is the debt or deal the document proves.

phrases.english: consecrated property is excluded, since "his fellow" is written.
phrases.notes: The פסוק says the thief pays double "to his fellow" (שמות 22:8), meaning another person, not the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from step 17 to list the categories it excludes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No כפל for land, slaves, documents, or הקדש.

steps.title: Maybe the shared feature is impurity of the carcass, which would leave out birds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a different shared feature of the listed items, a carcass that makes things impure by touching and carrying. That reading would leave birds out of כפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the shared feature is this: the specifics are things whose carcass makes impure by touching and carrying. If so, the rule would cover only such things, and not birds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's choice of shared feature. It proposes a different feature that would shrink the rule and leave birds out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלל ופרט וכלל includes only things similar to the specifics, so everything depends on which shared feature you pick. The ox, donkey, and sheep share another feature: their carcasses make things impure through touching and carrying. If that were the feature, birds would get no כפל, and that contradicts the broad rule.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, or perhaps: introduces a challenging alternative
The carcass of an animal that died without proper שחיטה

phrases.english: If so, just as the detail is clearly defined as
an item whose carcass makes impure by touching and carrying,
phrases.notes: The ה in square brackets is just a corrected spelling. It doesn't change the meaning.

phrases.english: so too any item whose carcass
makes impure by touching and carrying,
but birds, not!
phrases.notes: The challenge assumes a bird's carcass does not make impure this way, so birds would get no double payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the shared feature that step 17 drew from the specifics.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the shared feature of the specifics is 'movable and worth money in itself.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The specifics could just as well share a narrower feature, a carcass that makes impure by touching and carrying. That reading would exclude birds from כפל.

steps.title: But a garment is also in the list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggestion from step 19. The פסוק also lists שַׂלְמָה (a garment), and a garment has no carcass that could be טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really say that? But the פסוק writes 'garment'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that the items in the פסוק share the feature of a carcass that is טמא by touching and carrying. It points out that a garment is also in the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרט in the פסוק of כפל lists ox, donkey, sheep, and garment. A garment is not alive, so it can never become a נבלה. Carcass טומאה therefore cannot be the feature that all the listed items share.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really say this? (a pushback on a suggestion)
But it is written! (pointing to a פסוק that contradicts the idea)
A garment, one of the items listed in the פסוק of כפל

phrases.english: But can you really say this?
But "garment" is written!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ הָכִי? וְהָא שַׂלְמָה כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the alternate shared feature proposed in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the פרט's shared feature is a carcass that is טמא by touching and carrying.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פרט includes a garment, which has no carcass at all. So carcass טומאה cannot describe everything in the list.

steps.title: The carcass idea applies only among living creatures
steps.stepSummary: The reply limits the suggestion to living creatures. Among animals, those whose carcass is טמא would be covered, and those whose carcass is not would be left out. That would still exclude birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: We were speaking about living creatures. Say that among living creatures, a thing whose carcass makes things טמא by touching and by carrying is included, and a thing whose carcass does not make things טמא by touching and by carrying is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the garment problem by narrowing the claim. The carcass feature was only meant for the animals in the list, not for every item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The garment shows that non-living objects are covered by כפל. That does not settle which living creatures are covered. So the suggestion survives in a smaller form: among animals, only those whose carcass is טמא by touching and carrying would be included. Birds would still be left out, so the original worry stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (I could say), offering a possible reading

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not remove birds from כפל as a final ruling. It only rescues the challenge from step 19, so the question of birds is still open.

phrases.english: They say: We are speaking about living creatures;
say that among living creatures,

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁנִּבְלָתוֹ מְטַמְּאָ[ה] בְּמַגָּע וּבְמַשָּׂא – אִין,
phrases.english: a thing whose carcass makes things impure by touching and by carrying is included,
phrases.notes: The ה in square brackets is just a corrected spelling. It doesn't change the meaning.

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין נִבְלָתוֹ מְטַמְּאָ[ה] בְּמַגָּע וּבְמַשָּׂא – לָא,
phrases.english: a thing whose carcass does not make things impure by touching and by carrying is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20's garment objection by narrowing step 19's suggestion to living creatures.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the claim
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The carcass feature would have to describe every item in the פרט, so the garment disproves it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The carcass feature is only applied among living creatures. Birds could still be left out of כפל, so the challenge from step 19 stands.
